label: Zip Fly (Nylon)
note: Owner-uploaded reference images. Authoritative for construction/appearance; NOT usable as the tech-pack illustration (not line art, or shows multiple options).

references.evidence: A zip fly is unambiguous - open teeth chain plus slider, no fly buttons anywhere. What I cannot confirm at 239x318 px is the 'nylon (coil)' qualifier: the teeth read as a fine, flat, very low-profile chain (coil-like) but they catch a bright specular highlight, so a light metal chain is not fully excluded.

At 4x upscale a thin row of fine uniform coil teeth is visible below the waistband button, which establishes a zip (not button) fly; the rest of the zip is hidden behind the folded fly. Because only ~2 cm of chain is exposed, the nylon-vs-metal call and the full fly length are not verifiable here.

The zipper is plainly a coil/nylon chain: uniform continuous spiral teeth, matte black, dyed to match the tape, thin and flat against the cloth, with a black-coated slider - exactly the nylon coil fly the label describes, and clearly not a metal-tooth zip (no discrete shiny brass/nickel teeth). No fly buttons present, so it is not the button-fly sibling.
